sentences.text: Aisha Bello is a mental health social worker from the community mental health team.
Dr Shah, Callum's GP, requested the community mental health team to visit Callum.
Callum Reid is the person being assessed.
Callum's mother informed Aisha that she was at work when the visit occurred.
Callum has been feeling low since the summer.
Callum dropped out of college in September.
Callum was studying engineering at Level three.
Callum has been sleeping poorly, staying awake until 4 or 5 a.m. and sleeping during the day.
Callum has been eating little, mostly consuming toast, and has not eaten much since the summer.
Callum has asthma and uses an inhaler.
Callum was employed at a warehouse during Christmas as a temporary worker last year and has no current employment.
Callum's mother is a nurse who works night shifts.
Callum and his mother do not talk about his mental health or emotional state.
Callum's mother knows he is feeling low but does not know about the full extent of his emotional state.
Callum has no close friends he regularly talks to; he only communicates with online friend Josh and his sister, who is at university in Leeds.
Callum's dog, Bailey, is a staffy (Staffordshire terrier) and is three years old.
Callum's dog, Bailey, sleeps on his bed and is described as a 'good lad'.
Callum has no tablets stored in his flat; only paracetamol left in the kitchen belonging to his mother.
Callum has self-harmed by cutting his arms, which has occurred most nights for about two months.
Callum's arm cuts are not deep and have not required stitches or medical treatment for infection.
Callum has not taken an overdose of tablets or any medication.
Callum has considered ending his life and has said he wanted to die 'properly' in the last few weeks.
Callum went for a walk to Calder Bridge last week, where he stood and thought about jumping off the bridge.
Callum stated that his mother and his dog, Bailey, were the reasons he did not jump off the bridge.
The crisis team will visit Callum at home tomorrow to assess his safety and well-being.
The crisis team will visit Callum at home tomorrow, not in hospital, and will be a home-based team who visits more frequently than Aisha can.
Aisha will call Callum's mother with him at 6 p.m. that evening to inform her about his mental state and discuss keeping the paracetamol locked away.
Dr Shah's practice nurse will examine Callum's arm cuts on Thursday, the 26th.
Aisha will return to visit Callum on Monday, the 30th.
Aisha will contact the crisis team immediately after leaving the appointment to arrange the visit for tomorrow.
